config.title: useTransition

intro.title: useTransition
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple search interface that updates a list of items based on user input. You'll learn how to use the React useTransition hook to manage state updates that should be treated as non-urgent, preventing the UI from becoming unresponsive during slow updates. The main technologies involved are React, JavaScript, and JSX, focusing on hooks and functional components. By the end, you'll understand how to keep your app responsive by marking certain updates as transitions.
intro.usecase: The useTransition hook is essential for creating smooth user experiences in data-heavy applications like dashboards and e-commerce sites. When users apply filters to large datasets or search through product catalogs, useTransition prevents the UI from freezing during data processing. This pattern is commonly seen in admin panels where sorting/filtering operations need to happen without blocking interactions, and in forms with complex validation that shouldn't disrupt typing. By marking non-urgent updates as transitions, developers maintain responsive interfaces even during computationally expensive operations.

objectives: Initialize a useTransition hook to manage pending state during UI updates
Apply useTransition to wrap state updates that trigger slow rendering operations
Render conditional UI elements based on the pending status returned by useTransition
Configure a controlled input that maintains responsiveness during expensive filtering operations
Integrate useTransition with asynchronous data fetching to prevent UI blocking
Manipulate component state while preserving user interactions during transitions
Construct a search interface that remains responsive during computationally intensive filtering

steps.title: Import React and useTransition
steps.instruction: Import React and the useTransition hook from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useTransition from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useTransition hook are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: React and useTransition are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useTransition from 'react'. Check that your import statement includes both.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and useTransition from the 'react' package. The import statement should bring in these two items.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function App() {} or const App = () => {} and return <> </>.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useTransition } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named App and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state for data loading
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'isLoading' with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Call useState(false) and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'isLoading' initialized to false, ready to track loading status.
successCriteria: The useState hook is imported and used to declare 'isLoading' with initial value false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with false as the initial value and naming the variable 'isLoading'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to use useState to create a state variable named 'isLoading' with initial value false.

steps.title: Initialize useTransition
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useTransition hook and destructure the returned array to get 'isPending' and 'startTransition'.
steps.hint: Call useTransition() and destructure the array it returns into two variables: isPending and startTransition.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: destructuring from a hook
const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The useTransition hook is called and its return values are destructured into isPending and startTransition variables.
successCriteria: The useTransition hook is called and its return values are destructured into isPending and startTransition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useTransition() and destructuring the returned array into two variables named isPending and startTransition.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the App component, call useTransition() and destructure the array it returns into variables named isPending and startTransition.

steps.title: Create mock data loading function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create an async function named 'loadData' that simulates loading data.
steps.hint: Define an async function that uses the existing 'isLoading' state (you'll need to destructure it from useState).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an async 'loadData' function defined (though not yet called).
successCriteria: An async function named 'loadData' is defined inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you create an async function named 'loadData' inside the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create an async function named 'loadData' inside the App component.

steps.title: Create handler for loading with transition
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a function named 'handleLoadWithTransition' that calls startTransition with the loadData function inside.
steps.hint: The startTransition function is destructured from useTransition. It takes a callback where you can call your data loading function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handler function that wraps the data loading operation in startTransition to make it non-blocking.
successCriteria: The handleLoadWithTransition function is defined and calls startTransition with loadData inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it calls startTransition with loadData inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleLoadWithTransition that calls startTransition with loadData as its callback.

steps.title: Create handler for loading without transition
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'handleLoadWithoutTransition' that directly calls the existing 'loadData' function.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls loadData() without using startTransition.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function that loads data without using React's transition mechanism, allowing comparison with the transition-based approach.
successCriteria: A function named 'handleLoadWithoutTransition' is defined and calls 'loadData()'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named 'handleLoadWithoutTransition' that calls 'loadData()'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Create a function named 'handleLoadWithoutTransition' that calls 'loadData()'.

steps.title: Add loading status display
steps.instruction: In your component's return statement, add a <div> element that displays both the 'isLoading' and 'isPending' states with clear labels.
steps.hint: Inside the <div>, you can use JSX to show text like 'Loading: ' followed by the boolean value of isLoading, and similarly for isPending.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a <div> with two lines displaying the current values of isLoading and isPending.
successCriteria: A <div> element is added to the return statement that displays both isLoading and isPending values with descriptive labels.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some display, but make sure to show both isLoading and isPending with clear labels.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading status display wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added a <div> showing both state values.

steps.title: Add button for loading with transition
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Load with Transition' inside the div. Set its onClick handler to call the handleLoadWithTransition function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with onClick={handleLoadWithTransition} and the text content 'Load with Transition'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Load with Transition' appears in the UI, which when clicked triggers the transition-based loading.
successCriteria: The button element is present with text 'Load with Transition' and onClick is set to handleLoadWithTransition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a button with the exact text 'Load with Transition' and wired its onClick to handleLoadWithTransition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button for loading with transition is missing or incorrectly configured. Check that you've added the button element with the correct text and onClick handler.

steps.title: Add button for loading without transition
steps.instruction: In the return statement, add a button with the text 'Load without Transition' and wire its onClick to the handleLoadWithoutTransition handler.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with onClick={handleLoadWithoutTransition} and the text content 'Load without Transition'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have two buttons: one that triggers loading with transition and one that triggers loading without transition, allowing comparison.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Load without Transition' is present and its onClick is set to handleLoadWithoutTransition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the button text is exactly 'Load without Transition' and the onClick handler is correctly wired.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly configured. Check that you added a <button> element with the correct text and onClick handler.
